title: Search insert position (lower bound)
statement: Given a sorted array (possibly with duplicates), return the first index whose value is ≥ target (the position where target would be inserted to keep order). O(log n).
hints: Search over the half-open range [lo, hi) with the invariant: answer ∈ [lo, hi].
Predicate nums[mid] ≥ target is false…false true…true; find the first true.

solution.explanation: The universal template: find the first index where a monotone predicate (here nums[i] ≥ target) becomes true. Keep lo = first unknown, hi = first known true (initially n). If the predicate holds at mid, hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1. Stop when lo == hi. No off-by-one guesswork, and it handles duplicates and the empty array.
solution.python:
def search_insert(nums, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if nums[mid] < target: lo = mid + 1
        else: hi = mid
    return lo
